pages.sourcePdfText: Animals live all around us.
pages.sourceText: Animals live all around us.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Birds build their homes up high.
And so do bees.
pages.sourceText: Birds build their homes up high. And so do bees.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Spiders spin
their homes.
Tiny termites build
tall, tall homes.
pages.sourceText: Spiders spin their homes. Tiny termites build tall, tall homes.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Snails and tortoises grow
homes on their backs.
pages.sourceText: Snails and tortoises grow homes on their backs.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Fish live in the water.
Frogs can live in water and on land.
pages.sourceText: Fish live in the water. Frogs can live in water and on land.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Rabbits and rats live in
burrows under the ground.
pages.sourceText: Rabbits and rats live in burrows under the ground.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Monkeys and apes make
trees their homes.
pages.sourceText: Monkeys and apes make trees their homes.

pages.sourcePdfText: Bears and wolves live in dens.
pages.sourceText: Bears and wolves live in dens.

pages.sourcePdfText: Crocodiles live in swamps.
pages.sourceText: Crocodiles live in swamps.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Deer live in forests.
And so do tigers!
pages.sourceText: Deer live in forests. And so do tigers!

pages.sourcePdfText:
Some animals live close to us and
some live far away. 
But do you know what we have in
common with all the animals of the
world? 
One Large Home
We all build our homes in one large
home: planet Earth!

get a set of WHEELS to move
faster!

One kind of smell says, “Follow
me this way for a feast.”

pages.sourcePdfText: Another smell says, “Danger! Do not go there.”

pages.sourcePdfText: I love cakes and all kinds of sweets, just like you.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Want to see my muscles at work?
I may look very tiny to you, but I
am very strong.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Never mind if the door is shut. I
can slip through the smallest
crack.

pages.sourcePdfText: Believe it or not, hundreds of us live happily in a colony.

pages.sourcePdfText:
LET US LEARN SOME NEW WORDS.
Small - Big
Slow - Fast
Short - Tall
Thin - Fat
Hard - Soft
Noisy - Quiet
Here are some words with their opposites. Can you
make a sentence for each pair of opposite words?
For example, ‘An ant is small; an elephant is big’.
“As busy as an ant” is a nice way to describe
someone who is very hard working.

it?

pages.sourcePdfText: Cheena is my best friend. I wait for her to return from school.

pages.sourcePdfText: Sanju lives nearby. He teases me. It makes me very angry.

pages.sourcePdfText:
Tails can speak!
Did you know how animals and birds
tell us something by using their tails?
A dog wags its tail when it is happy. A
cat puffs up its tail when it is angry.
Often we say, “As clean as a cat”.
This is because cats do not like water,
yet they are always keeping
themselves clean by licking
themselves.

Crests are useful in many ways.They make
birds look attractive. Some birds can open

pages.sourceText: Do birds really have hair? Some birds look like they have hair on their heads. But their hair is not like ours. Instead, each hair is just a very thin feather. A group of such feathers is called a crest. Crests are useful in many ways.They make birds look attractive. Some birds can open and fold their crests to send signals to other birds. Some open their crests when they want to frighten away other birds and animals.

pages.sourcePdfText:
The hornbill’s helmet is called a casque
(rhymes with mask). Like ear-tufts and
crests, casques make hornbills look good.
This helps them find mates. A hornbill’s
casque also makes its beak stronger. With a
strong beak, hornbills can pick and eat
fruits more easily.
The furry worms on the owl’s head are
called ear-tufts. They are not really ears,
just bits of skin covered with feathers.
These help owls hide more easily, making
them look like they are part of a tree. The
ear-tufts also help them look attractive (to
other owls) or scary (to other birds and
animals).

The hornbill’s helmet is called a casque (rhymes with mask). Like ear-tufts and crests, casques make hornbills look good. This helps them find mates. A hornbill’s casque also makes its beak stronger. With a strong beak, hornbills can pick and eat fruits more easily.

Tide pools are shallow pools of seawater on rocky shores.

Where Does Energy Come From?
Energy comes from food.
Animals, including humans and birds, need energy to stay alive.
It allows our bodies to work and our brains to think.
Some birds have to eat every two hours, otherwise they wouldn’t
have enough energy to stay alive.
Bigger animals, like adult humans, can survive about two months
without any food, if they really have to. But to live well, we need to
eat many times a day!

pages.sourcePdfText:
Watch Where You Walk
The study of footprints is very interesting.
- Scientists have found marks of creatures that lived on Earth more
than 500 million years ago.
- People who hunt and gather food from the forest know how to
read animal tracks.
- Members of a community called the Irulas in South India can tell
the exact name of the snake simply by seeing its marks on the
ground.
- The next time you go to a forest, ask your guide to show you
animal tracks.
